headline: The CROWN Act of 2022 would have barred discrimination based on hair texture or hairstyle linked to a particular race or national origin, but the House voted it down on February 28, 2022.
what_it_does: If adopted, the bill would have prohibited discrimination based on a person's hair texture or hairstyle when that texture or style is commonly associated with a particular race or national origin. It would have covered people in federally assisted programs, housing, public accommodations, and employment. It would also have set enforcement procedures under the laws that already apply in those areas.

who_it_affects.group: People with natural hair textures or hairstyles commonly associated with a particular race or national origin
who_it_affects.how: They would have been protected from being treated unfairly because of their hair in covered areas.
They would have been barred from discriminating against workers or applicants based on protected hair textures or hairstyles.
They would have been barred from denying or limiting housing based on protected hair textures or hairstyles.
They would have been barred from refusing service or treating customers differently based on protected hair textures or hairstyles.

who_it_affects.group: Participants in federally assisted programs and the organizations that run them
who_it_affects.how: They would have been barred from discrimination based on protected hair textures or hairstyles in those programs.
